items.title: GTA 6's hand-crafted NPCs have over 600,000 animations compared to only 55,000 animations in GTA 5
items.excerpt: Rockstar's NPCs in GTA 6 carry more than 600,000 unique animations against GTA 5's 55,000 — a more than tenfold jump produced by a dedicated team art-directing individual crowd characters rather than generating them.
items.why: A hard number for what fully hand-authored character animation costs at AAA scale — the exact volume problem generative animation tools claim to solve.

items.title: Rockstar is 'at least 10 years ahead' of other games with GTA 6's NPC crowd technology, says dev behind 007 First Light's crowds
items.excerpt: A developer who built the crowd systems in 007 First Light says Rockstar's GTA 6 NPC crowd technology puts it roughly a decade ahead of the rest of the industry, in simulation depth rather than generative shortcuts.
items.why: Systemic, hand-built crowd simulation is currently outperforming LLM-driven NPC pitches — a useful reality check on where believable characters actually come from.

items.title: City Sample gets a major update with PCG and Unreal MCP workflows
items.excerpt: Epic's City Sample project has been rebuilt for Unreal Engine 5.8 with entirely new levels, plus additional toolsets, content and examples for procedural worldbuilding — including PCG and Unreal MCP (agent-driven editor) workflows.
items.why: Epic shipping an official MCP + procedural-generation reference project puts agentic tooling inside the engine's canonical sample — a direct template for how environment artists will actually work.

items.title: Inworld TTS Open Evaluation Toolkit: Reproducible TTS Evals
items.excerpt: Inworld open-sourced a framework for reproducible text-to-speech evaluation: local ASR, explicit normalization, per-sample measurements and offline reports that can be traced back to the source audio.
items.why: AI character voice is being adopted faster than it is being measured; an open eval harness gives audio directors a defensible way to judge synthetic voice before it ships in a game.

items.title: 1666: Amsterdam's developer says it 'won't be using any AI anymore', and the tech was only used 'in conception and pre-production'
items.excerpt: Assassin's Creed creator Patrice Desilets says his studio has dropped generative AI from 1666: Amsterdam after backlash, and that the tech had only been used in conception and pre-production — arguably the most creative phase of the whole process.
items.why: A named studio publicly reversing gen-AI use, and specifically naming ideation as the phase where it was used, is the sharpest current data point on where AI is and isn't welcome in a creative pipeline.

items.title: 'AI is just a plagiarism machine that makes people lose their jobs' in the eyes of The Talos Principle 3's writers
items.excerpt: The writers behind The Talos Principle 3 — a series literally about machine consciousness — explain why they refuse to use generative AI in their narrative work, calling it a plagiarism machine.
items.why: A narrative team whose subject matter is AI drawing a hard line on AI-assisted writing is a useful counterweight to the 'AI copilot for quest text' pitch.

items.title: 'Claude Strife': DLSS 5 has escaped into the wild, and things are immediately weird
items.excerpt: Nvidia's unreleased DLSS 5 neural rendering filter has leaked and modders are applying it to shipped games. It can look fine when used subtly, but heavier settings redraw character faces into something else entirely.
items.why: Neural rendering applied post-hoc to finished art means an AI model, not the art director, gets the last pass on a character's face — a real authorship problem for game art teams.

items.title: "The Half-Life 2 of AI" will change people's minds about AI, Saber exec says after CEO claims he'd happily replace a writer with AI
items.excerpt: Saber Interactive's CCO argues that a single genuinely great generative-AI game will flip public sentiment the way Half-Life 2 legitimised physics, following his CEO's remarks about replacing a fired writer with AI.
items.why: Frames the current stalemate as a craft problem rather than a tooling one: nobody has yet shipped a game where generative AI is the reason the game is good.

items.title: No, the Humankind 2 announcement trailer wasn't made with gen-AI, despite it sharing a similar kind of look
items.excerpt: Amplitude had to publicly deny that the Humankind 2 reveal trailer was generated, after viewers flagged its aesthetic as AI-looking. The studio says it used real actors, practical sets and custom-made props.
items.why: Hand-made work now has to prove it isn't machine-made — a new burden of proof landing on marketing and art teams.

items.title: Rockstar rules out GTA 6 microtransactions and AI – but there's still a catch
items.excerpt: Rockstar confirms GTA 6 will launch with no microtransactions and no generative AI, positioning the industry's biggest release as an explicitly hand-authored product.
items.why: The largest entertainment launch of the decade choosing 'no gen-AI' as a stated feature resets the default expectation for AAA production.

items.title: I Wish Rockstar Cared About People As Much As It Does GTA VI NPCs
items.excerpt: Rockstar's gameplay reveal leaned hard on hand-crafted NPC systems and per-character art direction; Aftermath argues you can't market artisanal craft while the people doing that craft are being crunched.
items.why: The strongest current articulation of the labour cost behind 'we did it by hand, not with AI' as a marketing position.

items.title: Here Are The Opening Night Live Games You Can Ignore Because Of GenAI Slop
items.excerpt: Kotaku audits the gamescom Opening Night Live lineup and catalogues which announced titles use generative AI — some already disclosed, many newly identified.
items.why: AI disclosure has become a review criterion applied to a whole showcase at once — a shift from case-by-case controversy to systematic audit.

items.title: Modders Have Been Playing Around With DLSS 5 And—Oh God, What The Hell Is That?!
items.excerpt: Kotaku surveys modder experiments with the leaked DLSS 5 neural filter: it 'works' for photoreal games, but anything stylized comes out mangled.
items.why: Concrete evidence that neural rendering is trained toward photorealism and actively destroys non-realist art direction — a live constraint for stylized games.

items.title: Nvidia DLSS 5's AI yassification filter reportedly escapes containment ahead of release
items.excerpt: Nvidia's DLSS 5 neural rendering for character models is reportedly running early, after modders extracted its files from NBA 2K27 ahead of the official launch.
items.why: Shows the driver layer becoming an uninvited art-direction pass that studios don't control and can't opt out of.

items.title: Leaked DLSS 5 Mod Shows Just How Much Nvidia's AI Filter Can Mess With Your Games
items.excerpt: An early build of Nvidia's AI-powered rendering suite confirms many of the fears raised at its initial reveal, with side-by-side comparisons showing heavy alteration of shipped art.
items.why: The most legible before/after documentation of what neural rendering does to authored assets.

items.title: NVIDIA's DLSS 5: Slop Or Not?
items.excerpt: 80 Level rounds up artist and developer reactions to people testing the leaked DLSS 5 neural filter across different games, weighing whether it is a legitimate rendering advance or generative noise.
items.why: A CG/art-community read on neural rendering rather than a hardware-press one — closest to how technical artists will actually evaluate it.

items.title: DLSS 5 Now Works on RTX 20 & 30 GPUs, Older Graphics APIs and Even PCSX2
items.excerpt: Modders have enabled NVIDIA's leaked DLSS 5 on RTX 20 and 30 series cards, older graphics APIs and even the PCSX2 emulator, extending neural rendering to games and hardware it was never targeted at.
items.why: Neural rendering spreading to legacy titles and emulators means decades of finished game art can be reinterpreted by a model without any developer involvement.

items.title: 5 takeaways from Gamescom 2026: A truly global show, AI's impact, Apple and Google's charm offensive
items.excerpt: PocketGamer.biz distils the key trends from gamescom 2026, with AI's practical impact on studio workflows among the dominant talking points of the show floor and business area.
items.why: A cross-section of where AI actually landed at the industry's biggest trade show, rather than a single vendor's pitch.

items.title: AI powering the global engine for game studios
items.excerpt: AWS senior gaming solutions architecture manager Huang Zhoubin breaks down how studios are actually operationalising AI — the infrastructure, workflow and production problems that sit between a model demo and a shipped feature.
items.why: Focuses on the unglamorous operational layer — how AI features get into a live production pipeline — which is where most studio adoption currently stalls.
